Governorship Election Presidential Gubernatorial Natasha Akpoti and Yahaya Bello
Former Kogi State Governor Yahaya Bello has dismissed the political threat posed by incumbent Kogi Central Senator, Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan, declaring that he will defeat the sitting senator “overwhelmingly” in the 2027 general election even without spending a dime.
Speaking during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today programme anchored by Seun Okinbaloye on Friday. Mr Bello boasted that his popularity across Kogi State remains unmatched despite being out of executive office for nearly four years, describing himself as a “political idol” to his constituents.
When asked whether Akpoti-Uduaghan’s grassroots mobilisation and recent street rallies posed a serious challenge to his senatorial ambition, the former governor brushed aside any comparison between himself and other contestants in the Kogi central district.
“Any other politician in Kogi State today—not even Kogi Central, let me say Kogi State—our polls are far apart when it comes to the contest,” Mr Bello stated.
“So leave anyone—any other contestant from Kogi Central—just put them aside. I’m talking of Kogi State,” he added.
Refusing to entertain questions about whether he would humbly accept defeat if Akpoti-Uduaghan prevailed at the polls, Mr Bello equated his political rivals in the district to “third-generation or fourth-generation” political mentees.
Asked directly if he was confident of victory, he replied: “Overwhelmingly.”

Mr Bello further claimed that his time away from the spotlight had only strengthened his bond with the electorate, claiming that Kogi Central District residents have already begun crowd-funding his senatorial bid with cash and agricultural produce.
Comparing his reception during a recent homecoming to that of the historic Ebira political figure, the late Alhaji Abdul Kokori Oziogu-Oziere, Mr Bello said constituents voluntarily gathered yams, farm produce, and money to urge him to represent them at the National Assembly.
“As I speak now, I will not spend one dime in the campaign and election, and by the grace of God, you’ll see me at the Red Chambers,” he said. “What I am today to the people of Kogi State and people of Kogi Central: I am their political idol. I did not mislead them. I did not betray them. I did not fail them, and as such, they want a repetition of that,” Mr Bello said despite ongoing corruption allegations against him after leaving office in 2024.
He added that his mission in the Senate would be to remain loyal to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) and ensure President Bola Tinubu’s policies and programmes reach the grassroots.
The looming 2027 showdown between the former governor and Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan sets the stage for what may be one of Nigeria’s fiercest senatorial battles. The contest is rooted in years of bitter political rivalry, legal tussles, and battles for supremacy in Kogi Central.
The animosity between both figures dates back to the 2019 and 2023 election cycles. In the 2023 senatorial race, Akpoti-Uduaghan (running on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP) faced off against Mr Bello’s anointed APC candidate, Abubakar Ohere.
Although INEC initially declared Mr Ohere the winner, the election petition tribunal and the Court of Appeal subsequently nullified his victory and declared Mrs Akpoti-Uduaghan the rightful winner—making her the first elected female senator from Kogi State.
Mr Bello, who governed Kogi State for two terms (2016–2024), relies heavily on established APC party machinery, incumbency influence through his successor Governor Usman Ododo, who is also from the district, and traditional political structures across Ebiraland.
Conversely, Akpoti-Uduaghan has built a populist, grassroots-driven brand anchored on vocal advocacy—notably her campaigns surrounding the revival of the Ajaokuta Steel Company—and direct community outreach.
Mrs Akpoti-Uduaghan’s resilience was tested in 2025 when she survived a contentious recall attempt following her suspension from the Senate. Her camp has welcomed Mr Bello’s entry into the 2027 race, framing the contest as a referendum against “godfatherism”.
Meanwhile, Mr Bello’s path to the ballot was recently solidified after the Federal High Court in Abuja dismissed a pre-election suit challenging his emergence as the APC’s Kogi Central senatorial candidate.
